transcript: Meeting header:
Time: 09:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Shah (Redwood); Tony Ramirez, Lena Cho, Amir Khan, Sophie Walker (Redwood internal)
Summary:

Quick internal sync between IT, Finance and Security on a handful of operational items: billing export access, KMS/encryption integration, audit log retention, SSO/SAML changes, and a short bench test for billing pipeline.
Topics:
- Billing export permission mapping and finance project IDs
- KMS integration for logs and compliance
- Audit log retention and SIEM routing
- SSO/SAML upcoming changes and impact to service accounts
- Light benchmark to validate export throughput
Transcript (timestamps approximate):
[09:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the admin sync. I'll kick us off. We have about 45 minutes. Main goal is to align on billing exports, KMS, audit logs and SSO rollout windows.
[09:01] Sophie: Yep, high level sounds good. We want to make sure the SSO changes don't break any service accounts used by the export pipeline.

[09:02] Tony: Quick context — billing export currently runs from a service acct that lives in the infra project, it's got Editor which is broader than we want. Finance would like a least-priv set up where we can still export daily CSVs.
[09:03] Lena: and also confirmation of which GCP project ids Redwood's billing connectors are writing to, that's the step we need to attach cost centers correctly.

[09:04] Jordan: Got it. Priya, quick note on how Redwood's hosted billing connector authenticates — it's via a service account key we rotate, but for dedicated/private customers we also support workload identity. There was a note earlier about KMS — we can wrap keys in your KMS or use our managed keys depending on compliance.

[09:05] Priya: yes, and I should flag that in the private deployments we often recommend customer-managed KMS, especially if SOC2/ISO controls require customer key custody. That said, it adds ops overhead for rotation and policy enforcement.

[09:06] Amir: If we go customer-managed KMS, we need to ensure our HSM/KMS audit events are delivered to the SIEM and there's no blind spot. Also, who will hold rotation ownership? Security prefers automated rotation with audit hooks.

[09:07] Jordan: Understood. We can provide automation scripts and a sample rotation playbook. We'll share the KMS integration doc after the call. (murmur) I'll also include examples for workload identity instead of long-lived keys.
[09:08] Tony: On the billing export permission, what exact iam roles does Redwood need to write the export? If it's too broad we need to scope it down. Right now it's Editor which is icky.

[09:09] Priya: For the connector to push to a GCS bucket we need storage.objectCreator and storage.bucketWriter on the bucket, and pubsub.publisher if we're using pubsub for events, we can provide a minimal role list in the doc.
[09:10] Lena: perfect, that helps. Also cost data mapping — we'll need the exact config fields Redwood uses in the export so finance can map to charge codes. A sample CSV header would be ideal.

[09:11] Jordan: We'll attach sample CSVs. I'll share them with your team. Quick note: previous transcriptions sometimes call our product 'Redwood Dedicatedy' or 'Redwood de-dic', so you'll see typos in docs — ignore those. Ha.

[09:12] Sophie: (laughing) noted. On SSO, our SAML provider is Okta, and we plan to roll a change that tightens assertion expiry and enforces MFA. I'm concerned about any scheduled jobs that rely on user tokens.

[09:13] Amir: Right, the export pipeline uses a service account so shouldn't be affected, but anything that uses delegated user credentials could break. We should inventory all places where user tokens are in use.
[09:14] Tony: do we have an inventory? we have a partial list but it's not complete; we can baseline this week.

[09:15] Jordan: let's make that an action. Tony and Lena, if you can confirm which exports and which projects, we'll scope the test. Priya — can you run a bench of the export flow to validate throughput so finance knows how long daily exports take?
[09:16] Priya: yes, I can put together a short benchmark run with a synthetic dataset that mirrors your daily volume. Should take less than a day to run and I'll share the steps.
[09:17] Lena: timeline wise finance needs exports consumed by the cost pipeline by the 25th, so we need the bench and permissions sorted well before that.
[09:18] Jordan: noted. On audit logs — Amir, you mentioned SIEM. What retention window do you need? And do you want all raw logs or filtered events?

[09:19] Amir: For now 13 months is the ask for audit retention, with privileged actions preserved longer. We want the raw audit events sent to the SIEM; we can filter downstream for storage cost but export raw first.

[09:20] Priya: Redwood can route audit events to your pubsub/S3/GCS endpoint; we'll include sample configs. One caveat: default retention in some platforms is shorter so we'll surface how to extend it and the cost implications.
[09:21] Sophie: cost is fine as long as the retention meets compliance. We need proof in the audit plan that logs are immutable and retained as required.
[09:22] Jordan: we'll include a short section in the doc about immutability options (bucket lock, object versioning) and recommended retention settings.
[09:23] Tony: what's the plan for rotation of credentials if we move to workload identity? Who updates the infra?

[09:24] Priya: workload identity ties cluster/service accounts to cloud identities — it reduces key rotation burden. We'll share a step-by-step and a small terraform snippet. If you want Redwood to manage it for a private install we can, but you'd need to grant the appropriate admin-like role.
[09:25] Amir: we prefer to manage keys; security won't allow Redwood to have key admin in prod. If Redwood needs to perform updates, we want a clear approval and change window.
[09:26] Jordan: understood — we'll design the playbook for customer-managed keys and a proposed change window for any required operations, and include rollback steps.

[09:27] Priya: quick note on the bench test — it's low risk. We'll try to keep it outside business hours; the test will write to a sandbox bucket and generate X rows to mirror your daily size, then show end-to-end time.
[09:28] Lena: okay, that should be fine. please share proposed test window and we'll confirm.

[09:29] Jordan: next steps: I'll send the KMS doc, minimal IAM role list, sample CSVs, and a bench test plan. Tony/Lena to confirm project ids and permissions. Amir/Sophie to review retention and SSO concerns.
[09:30] Sophie: one more thing — for compliance evidence, can Redwood provide a short diagram of log flows and access controls? We need that for the audit packet.
[09:31] Jordan: yes, we'll attach a simple diagram and a bullet list of controls. Priya will include the bench steps.
[09:32] Tony: do we need any legal sign-off for the change to service account roles?
[09:33] Sophie: likely not for scoping, but if it affects customer data residency or contract terms, legal should be looped. For now keep it to ops/security.
[09:34] Jordan: great. Any blockers?

[09:35] Amir: none immediate, just need the doc to verify things. also one tiny nit — sometimes audit logs show truncated service names, the parsing rule needs an update. I'll follow up with examples.
[09:36] Priya: please send examples; we can update the parsing rules in the export pipeline.
[09:37] Lena: ok, I'll pull sample CSV headers and send to Jordan and Priya.
[09:38] Jordan: perfect. We'll recap and assign the action items in the notes. Thanks everyone. We'll aim to have the docs and bench plan out by Monday.
[09:39] Sophie: thanks all, appreciate the quick sync.
[09:40] End of call
Notes: transcription may contain occasional mis-heard product names (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicatedy'); treat those as transcription artifacts.
Attachments referenced: KMS integration doc (to be shared), sample CSVs, bench test plan, IAM minimal role list.
